authority_basis.claim_scope: Normal force is a contact constraint force perpendicular to the surface and is not generally equal to weight.

concepts.statement: Normal force is determined by the contact constraint and other force components; it equals mg only in special configurations.
concepts.why_required: Normal force is a response imposed by contact geometry and dynamics, not a universal synonym for weight.
concepts.failure_if_omitted: Learners may set N=mg on inclines, accelerating systems or externally loaded contacts without checking the normal-axis dynamics.

symbols.name: signed net force along surface-normal axis

conditions: Contact is maintained while N is solved

model_conditions.condition: The body remains in contact with the surface while the normal force is modelled.
model_conditions.physical_reason: A compressive normal reaction exists only while the contact constraint is active.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: If the required normal force would be negative, contact is lost and N becomes zero under the unilateral-contact model.

model_conditions.condition: A surface-normal axis is declared before resolving forces that affect the contact constraint.
model_conditions.physical_reason: The normal force is perpendicular to the local contact surface.
model_conditions.failure_consequence: Weight or applied-force components can be projected incorrectly and N may be miscomputed.

representations.semantic_geometry: The contact surface fixes a local normal direction; the normal-force arrow is perpendicular to that surface and appears with all other forces affecting normal-axis dynamics.
must_not_imply: N is always equal to mg
the normal force exists after contact is lost
representations.verification_method: Resolve every force along the normal axis and verify the resulting N is compatible with the contact condition.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Draw the complete FBD without assuming a numerical value for the normal force.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: N=mg can be inserted as an unverified shortcut.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Choose the surface-normal axis and resolve all forces that project onto it.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: The contact constraint is not expressed in its natural direction.

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Use the normal-axis dynamics or constraint to solve N and check whether contact remains physically possible.
reasoning_sequence.failure_if_skipped: A special-case normal force can be mistaken for a general law.

required_transformations.description: Translate the contact surface into the local normal direction that constrains the reaction force.
Use all signed force components on the normal axis to solve the contact reaction rather than assuming N=mg.

misconceptions.incorrect_model: The normal force is always equal to mg.
misconceptions.why_plausible: A horizontal surface with no vertical acceleration and no other vertical forces gives N=mg, so the special case is easily overgeneralized.
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A block on an incline has N=mg cos(theta) in the simplest static case, not mg.
misconceptions.required_representation_repair: Show the surface-normal axis and resolve weight into normal and tangential components.
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Solve the surface-normal force balance or dynamics from the actual FBD.
misconceptions.verification: Substitute the solved N into the normal-axis equation and check the contact condition.

problem_families.name: Determine a normal contact force
problem_families.first_technical_move: Construct the FBD and choose the surface-normal axis without assuming N.
fatal_errors: setting N=mg without checking the normal-axis dynamics

problem_families.name: Dynamics on an inclined plane
problem_families.first_technical_move: Choose axes parallel and perpendicular to the surface after drawing the full FBD.
fatal_errors: using mg directly as normal force

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Replace normal-force constraint reasoning with a universal N=mg rule.
